properties.name: An Artifact registered with status PLANNED that REALIZES a capability is counted as BUILT: loop_status reported 7 "built" capabilities never checked, and the unrealized gaps turned into unverified ones — the status the 09-16 fix made writable is not read where "built" is decided
properties.source: graph-primitives design on flo2, loop_status and detect_gaps before and after, 2026-09-28
properties.statement:
OBSERVED 2026-09-28 in the graph-primitives design (flo2-hosted, reflow2 0.74.0), in a dev_reflow2 hub session closing gaps. Seven planned capabilities raised unrealized_capability. Four Artifacts were registered with add_artifact status: planned (name, description and location all saying "planned, not yet written") and linked with realizes to the seven. Then:
· loop_status: unexamined_claims 7, next "7 built capability(ies) never checked against reality (reconcile_artifacts)".
· detect_gaps: the seven unrealized_capability gaps disappeared and seven unverified_capability gaps appeared in their place.
Deleting the four Artifacts (and so the REALIZES edges) returned unexamined_claims to 0 and the unrealized gaps to the list.

So the sequel to this fact's fix is open: add_artifact now accepts `status` (absent means nobody said), and a caller can say PLANNED — but the computations that decide a capability is built (the unexamined-claims count, the unrealized/unverified gap pair, and plausibly the maturity 'realization' band, not checked) read the REALIZES edge and not the Artifact's status. A planned file therefore reads as delivered work.

NOT ESTABLISHED: which code paths ignore the status, and whether the maturity band and the delivery line do too — observed through loop_status and detect_gaps only, not traced. Workaround used: the planned locations were written into each capability's description instead of as Artifacts, and the unrealized gaps acknowledged as planned work.
